project.name: HDF5
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged ARVO workspace checkout `720e04e196aac60b8914830b0297fdf291cb7f00`, not metadata vulnerable_commit `65eff22348634144cd5a6e77159c27eb895d54b4`. The line anchors below are resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `H5F__cache_superblock_deserialize()` -> `H5G_ent_decode()` path shown in `patch.diff`.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. All source locations below refer to this exact snapshot.

bug_description.original: An out of bounds access occurs in `hdf5/src/H5Fint.c` at line 2859.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness writes a 148-byte HDF5 file whose superblock prefix decodes `super_vers = 1`, `sizeof_addr = 16`, and `sizeof_size = 32`. `H5F__cache_superblock_get_final_load_size()` trusts those bytes to compute a 164-byte superblock image, and `H5C__load_entry()` reallocates the heap buffer to that extent. In full deserialize, the same attacker-controlled widths are copied into `f->shared`, so `H5G_ent_decode()` uses 32-byte length fields and 16-byte addresses while decoding the root group symbol table entry. The root-entry header bytes make `ent->type = H5G_CACHED_STAB`, leaving only the final 16 bytes of the 164-byte image for the scratch pad. The vulnerable branch then evaluates `HDassert(2 * H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) <= H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH)` with a false predicate (`32 <= 16`), but in the reproduced build that assertion is not a runtime bounds check, so execution continues into two 16-byte scratch-pad decodes. The first decode consumes the last 16 bytes of the buffer, and the second starts with no bytes remaining. `H5F_addr_decode_len()` immediately executes `c = *(*pp)++`, producing the saved 1-byte AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read at `src/H5Fint.c:2859`.

source.description: First project parser read on the vulnerable path: the superblock prefix decoder consumes the on-disk version byte and materializes the dispatch key that later selects the legacy superblock layout.
source.value_from: The harness always reaches `H5Fopen` because `decider % 1 == 0`. It writes `poc[1:]` as the HDF5 file; in those written bytes, the first byte after the 8-byte HDF5 signature is `0x01`, so this statement sets `super_vers` to `1`.
source.note: This is the first project-code consumption of attacker-controlled file bytes that creates state later reused by the superblock-size calculation and the legacy deserialize branch.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The second scratch-pad address decode enters `H5F_addr_decode_len` with `*pp` already at the end of the 164-byte heap image, so the first byte fetch reads one byte past the allocation.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report is `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/H5Fint.c:2859` in `H5F_addr_decode_len`, reached from `H5G_ent_decode` line 148.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The `H5G_CACHED_STAB` path relies only on a debug assertion that two decoded addresses fit in the 16-byte scratch area. For the witness, `H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f)` is `16`, so the required 32 scratch bytes exceed `H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH`; because there is no runtime bounds check, execution continues into the pair of address decodes.
root_cause.note: The fix threads an end pointer into `H5G_ent_decode()` and adds `H5_IS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW(*pp, H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) * 2, p_end)` before these two calls, turning this unchecked layout assumption into a real runtime guard.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant widths originate here. The witness superblock prefix supplies `sizeof_addr = 16` and `sizeof_size = 32`, which later determine both the cache image length and how many bytes each downstream address or length decode consumes.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness passed signature lookup and superblock-prefix validation: the saved run reached full superblock deserialize, accepted `super_vers = 1`, `sizeof_addr = 16`, and `sizeof_size = 32`, and then continued into root-entry decoding.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 reproduced against staged checkout commit `720e04e196aac60b8914830b0297fdf291cb7f00`, not metadata vulnerable_commit `65eff22348634144cd5a6e77159c27eb895d54b4`; the line anchors here therefore target the staged tree actually used for reproduction.
`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 used only the saved source, patch, and ASan artifacts and did not instrument the ARVO workspace.

coarse_trace.summary: The superblock parser reads the witness version and size-width bytes, then trusts them to compute a 164-byte old-format superblock image.
The metadata cache reallocates the heap image to 164 bytes, and full superblock deserialize copies the attacker-controlled widths into `f->shared` for later decoders.

Root-group entry decode interprets the entry type as `H5G_CACHED_STAB`, reaches a scratch section with only 16 bytes left, evaluates a false debug-only size assertion, and still continues into two 16-byte address decodes.
The second scratch-pad address decode starts with no bytes remaining, and the first byte fetch overreads the heap image by one byte.

fine_trace.note: Source. Reads the on-disk superblock version byte from the witness and materializes `super_vers = 1`, the dispatch key later used by both the superblock-size calculation and the legacy deserialize branch.
Because step 1 selected the legacy prefix layout, the decoder reads the witness width bytes from the old-format offsets and stores `sizeof_addr = 16` and `sizeof_size = 32` in `sblock`.

Uses the tainted version and width fields from steps 1-2 to compute the full speculative superblock image length. For witness values `super_vers = 1`, `sizeof_addr = 16`, and `sizeof_size = 32`, the source macros resolve `actual_len` to 164 bytes.

ASan allocation context. The metadata cache reallocates the superblock image using `actual_len + H5C_IMAGE_EXTRA_SPACE`; in the saved ASan run, the resulting heap region is exactly 164 bytes (`[0x60f000000040, 0x60f0000000e4)`). The report identifies this reallocation site as the allocation context for the overread buffer.

In the legacy superblock branch taken because `super_vers = 1`, full deserialize copies the attacker-controlled widths into `f->shared`. From this point on, `H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f)` is 16 and `H5F_SIZEOF_SIZE(f)` is 32 for every downstream decode.

When `H5F__cache_superblock_deserialize()` calls `H5G_ent_decode()` for the root group entry, these reads consume a 32-byte name offset, a 16-byte header address, and an entry type of `1`, so `ent->type` becomes `H5G_CACHED_STAB`. Because the root entry begins 92 bytes into the 164-byte image, this leaves only the final 16 bytes of the buffer for the scratch-pad section.

Root cause. For this witness, `2 * H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f)` is 32 while `H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH` is 16, so the scratch layout assumption is already false before any scratch-pad decode starts. In the reproduced build this `HDassert` is not a runtime rejection or bounds check, as shown by the saved ASan stack reaching line 148, so execution still proceeds into the two scratch-pad address decodes.

With `ent->type == H5G_CACHED_STAB` and no runtime bounds check on the scratch area, the first scratch-pad decode uses the remaining 16 bytes of the heap image to materialize `btree_addr`, advancing `*pp` from the scratch-pad start to exactly the end of the 164-byte buffer.

The second scratch-pad address decode is entered immediately after step 8, so `*pp` already equals the end of the 164-byte heap image and no bytes remain. There is still no runtime bounds check before this second call.

Sink. `H5F_addr_decode_len()` begins the second 16-byte address decode with `*pp` at the end of the 164-byte heap buffer, so this first byte fetch reads address `0x60f0000000e4`, one byte past the allocation. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan allocation stack reports `H5MM_realloc -> H5C__load_entry` here before the overread in the superblock image.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: allocation_context provides the heap extent; the root cause is the missing runtime bounds check in H5G_ent_decode.

format.name: HDF5 file (h5_read_fuzzer witness)
format.contract: The staged input is 149 bytes: one leading fuzzer decider byte plus a 148-byte HDF5 file. Because `decider % 1 == 0`, the harness always calls `H5Fopen` on the written file. The HDF5 bytes must encode a version-1 superblock whose old-format prefix yields `sizeof_addr = 16` and `sizeof_size = 32`, and whose root-group symbol-table entry decodes `cache_type = 1` (`H5G_CACHED_STAB`). Those exact witness values make HDF5 allocate a 164-byte superblock image, leave only 16 bytes for the root-entry scratch pad, consume those 16 bytes in the first scratch-pad address decode, and start the second address decode at the end of the heap buffer.
